title: Euclidean distance geometry and the orthogonal beltway problem
summary: The orthogonal beltway problem is the problem of recovering the $\mathrm{O}(n)$-orbit of a $δ$-function supported at a finite number of points in $\r^n$ from its auto-correlation or, equivalently, second moment. It was introduced as a generalization of the classical beltway problem in X-ray crystallography and was motivated by cryo-electron microscopy. In this paper we prove that if $m > n$, then the $\mathrm{O}(n)$-orbit of generic binary signal supported at $m$ points where at least $\ell$ of them have equal magnitude can be recovered from its auto-correlation.
